limits.reason: un ton ferme: both the noun ferme (farm) and the adjective are listed and the adjective reading is given, but the rules do not yet put an adjective first after a noun whose own first reading had to be decided by context (ton: your / tone).
Je te suis partout: suis is être or suivre and both readings are given; an object pronoun before it does not decide (je te suis reconnaissant is être), only the meaning does.
Les vers mangent la terre: vers is verse(s) or the plural of ver (worm); both readings are given and only the meaning of the sentence decides.
Elle coupe les fils: fils is son(s) or the plural of fil (thread); both readings are given and only the meaning of the sentence decides.
Il vit la mer et sourit: vit is the present of vivre or the passé simple of voir, and sourit is ambiguous in the same way, so the sentence has no verb that is plainly past; both readings are given.
